probes.question: What does DNS do?
options: Turns a website name into an IP address

probes.question: True or false: a website's IP address may vary depending on where you are.

image.alt: A black rotary telephone on a desk beside a small student telephone directory booklet, in an old black-and-white photo.
image.credit: University of Alberta Archives Photographs Collection - https://archive.org/details/UAA-1972-058-974 / Wikimedia Commons

body.claim: When you type a website name, a system called DNS looks up its numeric address for you.
body.why: Computers find each other by IP addresses, which are numbers like 192.0.2.172. DNS uses special servers to match a name you can remember, like mozilla.org, to the real address. Large sites run on multiple servers, so the address you get may vary depending on where you are.
